scope: Historical frozen 140997 only. Later packed-publication and epoch-restoration source changes are excluded.

raw_archive.status: local raw evidence; pending v2 archive
raw_archive.retention: All 540 original rows, source snapshots, complete current and historical object inventories, symbols, native oracle outputs and blobs remain in the hash-addressed raw runs; deliberately not duplicated in this summary.

limitations: Six sequential blocks in one host window per mode, balanced rotated arm permutations; check and O2 measured separately, OS caches not flushed. This is one fixed synthetic workload, not general language/workload coverage or a significance test.

Zil wall is resident request send-to-response, excluding process startup. Rust wall includes a fresh Cargo process and any rustc subprocess startup. Source writes, inventory/symbol extraction and native execution are outside request wall.

Resident own CPU and resident+waited-child CPU are /proc deltas with kernel tick resolution; they are not per-phase counters. Rust CPU is wait4 user+system for the Cargo invocation and waited children; scopes differ.

Resident RSS is the Zil root process at response; resident peak is a cumulative process high water mark across earlier parent requests. Cargo sampled peak is only the Cargo root; wait4 maxrss is a largest-process statistic, not simultaneous process-tree sum. No cross-language memory advantage follows.

Rust 1.99.1 commit 58cf8f9c35b355199727627d07ae34a4e2846d67 embeds LLVM 23.1.1; Zil uses LLVM API/clang 23.1.4. Same requested CGU16/O2/jobs1 does not make partition membership, optimizer, frontend work or verification equivalent.

Actual current Rust incremental session objects are selected by unique completed-session delta or retained previous current session; historical sessions are excluded. Matching inode/device/mtime/content is a physical carry-forward observation, not rustc query-red-green or proof of skipped codegen. Zil hit states are current compiler cache receipts, not the same metric.

Defined nm symbols document emitted object contents, which can omit optimized/inlined source functions; they are not complete source dependency sets. Equal hashes alone do not prove that work was skipped.
Current independent Zil Verify is invoked on every successful request; cached process-private receipts can discharge current obligations. Rust and Zil safety/diagnostic contracts are different.
No claim of globally minimal work, whole-pipeline completion, Rust equivalence or universal speedup. Cold/broad overhead and error/recovery gaps remain visible.

work: Candidate private edit still executes 5/425 Types CFGs and 21 BodyKeys, although it lowers 1 machine function and independently checks 1 function proof. It is not end-to-end one-function work.

Candidate measured error is a Types rejection, preserving existing executable; in recovery it executes 404/425 Types CFGs and 421 BodyKeys, despite native lower/proof counts 1 and object misses 1. Parent-history accelerator restoration is a real remaining defect in this frozen source.

protocol.timing_policy: Sequential three-arm requests, six balanced arm permutations rotated per block/request. Zil resident send-to-response excludes startup; Rust full Cargo process includes startup. Source writes, object inventory and native execution occur outside request wall timing. No profiling. OS cache not flushed.
protocol.parent_policy: Every non-cold request is immediately preceded for all three arms by its validated named parent: recovery<-error, restore<-private, all others<-cold. Preparations retained and validated, no cache reset within block.
protocol.inventory_policy: Archive actual object bytes and defined symbol tables, Rust incremental metadata and inode/content/mtime observations; Zil current per-unit action-key/cache-state receipts. Hash equality is not proof of skipped work. No partition equivalence implied by requested CGU16.
protocol.memory_policy: Root-only RSS; resident Zil root vs Cargo root are different scopes. wait4 maxrss is largest process, not tree sum; no cross-language memory advantage.
